mechanism_claims.claim_text: Cg-BigDef1[1-93] and the N-terminal domain Cg-BigDef1[1-42] form bacterially triggered fibers/nanonets that entrap S. aureus, while the C-terminal beta-defensin-like domain alone does not show this nanonet phenotype under the tested condition.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Nanonet assembly is directly observed for S. aureus assays; do not generalize to all targets without additional source evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Cg-BigDef1[1-93] kills S. aureus SG511 without detectable Sytox Green membrane permeabilization at the source-tested concentrations/time course.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is a negative membrane-permeabilization finding in S. aureus SG511, not proof of no membrane effects in every organism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The N-terminal hydrophobic domain is required for salt-stable antimicrobial behavior and nanonet assembly; hydrophobic bacterial interaction is a source-discussed interpretation, not a standalone direct assay endpoint.
